name: machine-failure-prediction
description: Machine failure prediction using Gradient Boosting machine learning with an interactive Streamlit dashboard.

paragraphs: An AI-powered predictive maintenance system that detects machine failures from live sensor readings, using a Gradient Boosting classifier trained on the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance dataset — with live prediction, risk scoring, batch analysis, rule-based failure explanation, and downloadable reporting.
98.75% accuracy sits next to 83% precision and 79% recall — that gap isn't a modeling mistake, it's a direct consequence of the dataset's shape:

1. Severe class imbalance. Only 339 of 10,000 machines (3.39%) actually fail. A model can score 96%+ accuracy just by predicting "no failure" every time — accuracy is a misleading headline number here. Precision and recall are the honest metrics, because both are computed only over the rare positive class.
features: Live Detection — enter a single machine's sensor readings manually and get an instant failure probability, risk score, and risk level

Rule-Based Explanation Engine — explains why a reading looks risky using the AI4I dataset's own documented failure-mode formulas (heat dissipation, power, overstrain, tool wear) — verified to match the dataset's…
Batch Analysis — score a sample of the holdout set or upload your own CSV of machine readings, with filterable results and auto-generated reports
Security/Maintenance Report Generator — downloadable TXT, CSV, and PDF reports summarizing flagged machines and the top reasons behind them
Model Performance Dashboard — confusion matrix, ROC curve, Precision-Recall curve, and feature importance, all computed live from the frozen model on the untouched final holdout set
